issues.legal_issue: A superior court may set aside bail granted pending appeal when the lower court fails to give case-specific reasons and ignores material factors relevant to the accused’s release.
material_facts: The accused had been convicted of a grave offence and sentenced to life imprisonment; his appeal against the conviction was pending.

The trial court had considered testimony from three eyewitnesses and evidence of a prior grudge and a threat to eliminate the deceased when finding the accused guilty of participating in a conspiracy.
The accused had spent only nine months in custody before bail was granted.
The record described numerous criminal cases against the accused, with several still pending; the complainant and the State also raised concerns about threats to witnesses.

The High Court recorded the parties’ submissions and the State’s opposition but granted bail without identifying reasons or showing that it had weighed the seriousness of the offence, the conviction and sentence, the accused’s antecedents, or other relevant material.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had not exercised its discretion judicially: its order was cryptic, gave no reasons, and failed to consider relevant material. The Supreme Court set aside the bail order, cancelled the bail bonds, and directed the accused to surrender. The decision did not determine the merits of the pending conviction appeal and did not prevent a fresh bail application if new circumstances arose.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, bail is discretionary but must be granted judicially, not as a matter of course. A court must consider relevant factors including the nature and gravity of the accusation, the likely punishment, the supporting material, the accused’s antecedents and conduct, and risks to witnesses or the administration of justice. A bail order, particularly for a serious offence, must state reasons sufficient to show a prima facie basis for the decision; it need not undertake a detailed assessment of the evidence. An appellate court reviewing the original grant of bail may set it aside when discretion was exercised arbitrarily, without application of mind, or after ignoring relevant material; that review is distinct from cancellation based on later misconduct or supervening circumstances. The Court relied on Ram Govind Upadhyay v. Sudarshan Singh (2002) 3 SCC 598, Prasanta Kumar Sarkar v. Ashis Chatterjee (2010) 14 SCC 496, Puran v. Rambilas (2001) 6 SCC 338, Kalyan Chandra Sarkar v. Rajesh Ranjan (2004) 7 SCC 528, Mahipal v. Rajesh Kumar (2020) 2 SCC 118, Prakash Kadam v. Ramprasad Vishwanath Gupta (2011) 6 SCC 189, Neeru Yadav v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2014) 16 SCC 508, and Imran v. Mohammed Bhava (2022) SCC OnLine SC 496.

rule.if: appeal_against_bail_grant and pending_appeal_after_conviction and grave_offence_conviction and severe_sentence_imposed and short_custody_before_bail and serious_criminal_antecedents and bail_order_gave_no_case_specific_reasons and lower_court_ignored_relevant_material

predicates.appeal_against_bail_grant: A party asks a superior court to review a lower court’s order granting bail.
predicates.pending_appeal_after_conviction: The accused’s appeal against a conviction is pending while release on bail is sought.
predicates.grave_offence_conviction: The trial court convicted the accused of a grave offence.
predicates.severe_sentence_imposed: The trial court imposed a severe sentence on the accused.
predicates.short_custody_before_bail: The accused had spent only a short time in custody before the lower court granted bail.
predicates.serious_criminal_antecedents: The record showed numerous criminal cases involving the accused, including cases still pending.
predicates.bail_order_gave_no_case_specific_reasons: The lower court granted bail without explaining which case-specific considerations supported release.
predicates.lower_court_ignored_relevant_material: The lower court failed to account for material concerning the offence, conviction, sentence, antecedents, or risks relevant to release.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges bail granted to a convicted person awaiting appeal and the specified aggravating facts and defects in the lower court’s reasoning are present, the bail grant is set aside.
